problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{7\pi }{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{4}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Containing the Tangent Function Transformed by Multiple Operations
examples.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3})-2 & =0 \\ 2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3}) & =2 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{3} & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(6n-1)\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0, \pm 1, \pm 2,\ldots$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0 \leq x \lt 2\pi.$ Notice that setting $n=0$ gives a result outside of the domain.

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\dfrac{5\pi}{12}.$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\dfrac{11\pi}{12}.$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\dfrac{17\pi}{12}.$

- Setting $n=4$ gives $x=\dfrac{23\pi}{12}.$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0 \leq x \lt 2\pi.$ So, the solutions $x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x = \dfrac{5\pi}{12}, \dfrac{11\pi}{12}, \dfrac{17\pi}{12}, \dfrac{23\pi}{12} .
$$

$$

Solving our equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{3} \\ x & =\frac{(4n-1)\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{7\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\frac{11\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=4$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{4}$

- Setting $n=5$ gives $x=\frac{19\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=6$ gives $x=\frac{23\pi }{12}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{4},\,\,{x}_{2}=\frac{7\pi }{12},\,\,{x}_{3}=\frac{11\pi }{12},\,\,{x}_{4}=\frac{5\pi }{4},\,\,{x}_{5}=\frac{19\pi }{12},\,\,{x}_{6}=\frac{23\pi }{12}.
$$
